proof:
# A volume-ratio gluing theorem with an arbitrary middle body

This is a scoped three-fiber theorem, not the unrestricted OC statement.

Let d>=1, let K be a full-dimensional compact convex body in R^d with centroid zero and volume V, and let 0<r<=s. At integer bases -1 and1 place translated copies of rK and sK. Let the actual middle fiber B be any full-dimensional compact convex body containing their Minkowski average, and suppose these are the only nonempty integer fibers. There is no homothety, symmetry, or centroid condition on B.

Write a=r^d V, b=s^d V and U=|B|. If

    b/a <= (3+sqrt(5))/2,                              (1)

then the source has a deterministic point on its actual middle fiber with every closed ambient containing halfspace of mass at least

    (Gamma_d/2)(a+b+U).                                (2)

A stronger exact sufficient condition follows from the unequal-scale interpolation theorem below.

## 1. A common point retaining the endpoint and middle contributions

A continuous shear depending affinely on the integer base centers both endpoint copies at zero. Explicitly, if their translations are c_- and c_+, subtract (c_-+c_+)/2+z(c_+-c_-)/2 from x. This preserves integer bases, each d-dimensional fiber volume, and all ambient halfspaces. The transformed middle body contains

    D=((r+s)/2)K.

Its centroid zero is one actual middle point. Both endpoints contain the smaller centered copy rK. For a nonvertical cap through (0,0), the two endpoint thresholds on these retained equal copies are opposite. The proved paired-centroid-tail theorem gives endpoint mass at least2 Gamma_d a. The middle's retained D supplies at least Gamma_d |D|. Thus at this SAME point every such cap has mass at least

    Gamma_d (|D|+2a).                                 (3)

A vertical cap through the middle contains all of D in its middle fiber and at least one whole rK endpoint copy. Its mass is at least |D|+a, which is no smaller than (3), since Gamma_d<=1/2. Moving a containing cap to pass through the point can only decrease mass, so (3) holds for every closed ambient containing halfspace.

The elementary arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives

    |D|=((r+s)/2)^d V >= sqrt(ab).

With t=sqrt(b/a), condition (1) is precisely t^2-t-1<=0. Consequently

    |D|+2a >= sqrt(ab)+2a >= a+b.                     (4)

Equations (3)--(4) give depth at least Gamma_d(a+b) at the actual point zero.

## 2. Choosing one actual point, for every middle volume

If U<=a+b, choose that point zero. Its bound Gamma_d(a+b) is at least the target (2). If U>=a+b, choose the ordinary centroid of the ACTUAL middle body B. Its own-fiber Grünbaum bound Gamma_d U is at least (2), and the other fibers contribute nonnegative mass. Equality of the two masses permits either choice.

This is a deterministic two-case selection, not an average of centers. In particular an arbitrarily enlarged or displaced compatible middle body is covered: its actual volume decides the case. Transforming back by the stated shear keeps the chosen point on the original integer middle fiber.

## 3. Stronger sufficient condition from source interpolation

Define the normalized endpoint budget P_d(r,s) by

    P_1(r,s)=r;
    P_d(r,s)=[r c_d+(s-r)(1-c_d)/(d-1)]^d,
              d>=2, r<=s<=dr, c_d=(2 Gamma_d)^(1/d);
    P_d(r,s)=r^d, d>=2, s>=dr.

The universal interpolation theorem in candidate cd9374750b11bd94 proves endpoint mass at least V P_d(r,s) at the same midpoint centroid. Thus (3) improves to

    Gamma_d |D|+V P_d(r,s).

The same two-case proof establishes (2) whenever

    ((r+s)/2)^d+P_d(r,s)/Gamma_d >= r^d+s^d.           (5)

This states an explicit sufficient scalar condition. No claim is made that (5) is necessary, that it holds for all scale ratios, or that failure of (5) gives a depth counterexample. Condition (1) is the simpler uniform corollary proved directly above from the already established equal-copy paired theorem.

All fibers in this note have positive full d-volume. The d=1 case uses Gamma_1=1/2 and the exact interval pair budget, and no d-1 denominator is used there. Lower-dimensional intrinsic fibers, more than three integer fibers, and arbitrary nonhomothetic endpoint shapes require separate arguments and are not included by analogy.
